column1: # title: ENG-205 Middle Ages Intro — 5 Q&A
What are the three sub-periods of medieval English literature?
column2: The three sub-periods are the Anglo-Saxon, the Anglo-Norman, and the Middle English periods.

column1: What event made French the language of England's ruling class?
column2: William the Conqueror's Norman Conquest of 1066 made French the language of England's ruling class.

column1: Which four languages circulated in Anglo-Norman England?
column2: Old French, Latin, Old English, and the Celtic languages all circulated in Anglo-Norman England.

column1: Does Old English poetry rely on rhyme or alliteration?
column2: Old English poetry links its lines through alliteration and rarely uses rhyme.
A kenning is a two-word compound that replaces a plain noun, such as "life-house" for the body.

column1: In the heroic code, what does the lord owe his men?
column2: The lord owes his men generosity in the form of gifts, treasure, and protection.

column1: In the heroic code, what do the men owe their lord?
column2: The men owe their lord loyalty to the death and revenge if he is killed.

column1: What tone is typical of Old English poetry?
column2: Old English poetry is typically elegiac, a mournful tone that mixes pagan heroic values with Christian ones.

column1: What is the earliest poem recorded in English?
column2: Caedmon's Hymn is the earliest poem recorded in English.
Bede preserved Caedmon's Hymn by including it in his Ecclesiastical History of the English People.

column1: Where did the romance form come from?
column2: The romance form grew out of Celtic Breton lays that Anglo-Norman aristocrats loved.

column1: Which famous romance survives in only one manuscript?
column2: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight survives in only one manuscript.
Sir Thomas Malory wrote Le Morte Darthur while in prison around 1470.
William Caxton printed Le Morte Darthur in 1485.

column1: How did the Black Death (1348) change English society?
column2: By killing a quarter to a third of the population, the Black Death created a labor shortage that let survivors move up socially.

column1: What did social mobility after the Black Death lead to?
column2: Mobility after the plague produced a rising merchant class, the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, and new criticism of the Church and society.
The Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe who criticized Church corruption and produced the first complete English Bible around 1380.

column1: What verse form does Chaucer mainly use in The Canterbury Tales?
column2: In The Canterbury Tales, Chaucer mainly uses rhymed couplets with five-stress lines.
The Alliterative Revival was a 1300s return to Old English alliterative verse, seen in Sir Gawain and the Green Knight and Piers Plowman.
A mystery play acts out a Bible story as one play in a cycle.
A morality play shows personified virtues and vices fighting over a soul, as in Everyman.
Caxton's moveable type produced identical copies quickly, which spread texts widely and helped fix spelling standards.

column1: Who was the first true English king?
column2: Alfred the Great, who reigned from 871 to 899, was the first true English king.
The shared threat from the Vikings, or Danes, united the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms.
No, Shakespeare wrote in Early Modern English, while Old English is the language of Beowulf and Middle English is the language of Chaucer.

column1: Why does English use different words for an animal and its meat, such as cow and beef?
column2: English-speaking peasants raised the animals while French-speaking Norman lords ate the meat, so "cow," "sheep," and "swine" are English words but "beef," "mutton," and "pork" are French.
